events.title: The election of Pope Innocent III
events.shortBlurb: The cardinals chose Lotario dei Conti di Segni, who as Innocent III would raise the medieval papacy to the height of its power…
body: Born about 1161 at Gavignano in the Roman Campagna, Lotario dei Conti di Segni studied theology at Paris and law at Bologna and was made a cardinal at twenty-nine. On 8 January 1198, the day Celestine III died, the cardinals elected him pope, and he took the name Innocent III.

His eighteen-year pontificate raised the medieval papacy to its height. He styled himself the vicar of Christ, arbitrated between rival claimants to the empire, laid England under an interdict in the quarrel over Stephen Langton, and saw the Fourth Crusade, preached at his call, diverted to the sack of Constantinople in 1204.

He gave a first approval to the followers of Francis of Assisi in 1209 and to those of Dominic in 1215, and in November of that year he opened the Fourth Lateran Council, which defined the faith against the Albigenses and bound every Christian to annual confession. He died at Perugia on 16 July 1216.
